<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Now I'll implement everything. Let me create:

Creating boardWindow.xhtml and src/extras/boardWindow.ts.

Next steps include locale files, config updates, and heavy refactoring of board.ts. Commands, addon, hooks, data.ts, CSS, and README also need updates. The Board class will track hostWin, mainWin, and a host type to distinguish tab from window mode.

The plan uses a `boards` map keyed by host window. Popping out requires destroying the tab board, closing the tab, opening a chrome window, and remounting. The map must be rekeyed when switching between tab and window modes.

The `popOut` method will unmount the board without destroying the scene, remove the entry from the `boards` map, open a new chrome window, and remount the board there. The `Board` constructor is being redesigned to accept only `mainWin` and track the host type, host window, tab ID, and chrome window internally.

The `Board` class will expose an `isOpen` getter and a `mapKey` property to identify the correct host window for the `boards` map. A `destroyed` flag is needed so that unmounting for a pop-out does not permanently destroy the board. The `unmount` method will clean up scene subscriptions, resize observers, interactions, and the renderer without marking the board as destroyed, allowing it to be remounted later.

`destroy()` will call `unmount` with both close flags and set `destroyed` to true. `openAsWindow` will focus an existing chrome window or pop out from the current tab. Commands will prevent duplicate boards.

A `findOpenBoard` helper will scan the `boards` map for any active board. The `openBoard` API will reuse an existing board if one is already open, otherwise create a new instance and mount it in a tab. The `openBoardWindow` API will follow the same pattern.

The `openBoardWindow` command will focus an existing window board, pop out a tab board, or create a new window board. The `popOut` method will delete the board from the `boards` map using its old key before remounting it in a chrome window and inserting it under the new key.

The chrome window will register an unload listener to destroy the board when the user closes it. The extras script for the window will only set the window title and resolve its initialization promise, deferring the actual mount to the main plugin. The script path will use the `__addonRef__` placeholder, which the scaffold replaces when bundling assets.

The extras script will be bundled directly into `addon/content/scripts/` without a `chrome/` subdirectory, since the addon registers content at the root `content/` path. The esbuild configuration targets `firefox115` and outputs to `.scaffold/build/addon/content/scripts`. Next, I will implement `addItems` with position support.

The `addItems` method will accept an optional `at` coordinate. When provided, the first item will anchor at that exact spot, and subsequent items will shift by card width and height plus grid gaps. A new `freeSpotNear` helper is being considered to simplify this grid-based placement logic.

The `freeSpotNear` helper now places items in a 4×4 grid around a base point, defaulting to the camera position plus 60 pixels. It then calls `findFreeSpot` to locate the nearest open cell. A `bindDrop` method is being added to the board to handle drag-and-drop events, including preventing default behavior and setting the drop effect to copy.

The drop handler adds a CSS class to the board root while dragging over it, removes the class when the cursor leaves the board, and converts the drop position from screen coordinates to world coordinates using the renderer.

The drop handler converts screen coordinates to world coordinates using the canvas bounding rect, then delegates to `handleItemDrop` to load the library and add the items. A `getDraggedItems` helper parses the `DataTransfer` object by reading `Zotero.DragDrop.getDataFromDataTransfer` and extracting item IDs from the `zotero/item` or `item` data type.

The `getDraggedItems` helper now falls back to parsing the raw `zotero/item` string if the structured drag data is missing. During dragover, only the data type check is used because `getData` can be empty in some browsers for security reasons. If dropped items belong to a different library, that library will be loaded before adding them. The pop-out and dock toolbar buttons will use custom SVG icons.

The SVG path definitions for the pop-out and dock icons are now set. Next, I will verify how `freeSpotNearCamera` uses `CARD_H`.
</details></think>

Pop-out and library drag-drop are in place. Build and typecheck both pass.

**Pop-out / dock**
- Tools → **Open Spatial Workspace in Window**, or the toolbar **Pop out** button, opens a resizable chrome window you can put beside the library
- **Dock** returns it to a tab
- Tab remains the default for Tools → Open Spatial Workspace / `Ctrl+Shift+W`

**Drag-and-drop**
- Dropping library items (`zotero/item`) onto the board (tab or window) adds them via `DataBridge.addItems`
- Cards land at the drop’s world position
- Context-menu add still works

**Key files**
- [`addon/content/boardWindow.xhtml`](addon/content/boardWindow.xhtml) + [`src/extras/boardWindow.ts`](src/extras/boardWindow.ts) — chrome shell
- [`src/modules/board.ts`](src/modules/board.ts) — tab/window host, popOut/dock, drop target
- [`src/modules/commands.ts`](src/modules/commands.ts) — menus + `openBoardWindow`
- [`src/modules/data.ts`](src/modules/data.ts) — optional drop-position for `addItems`
